answer: An agent economy can bind voting and reputation to a scarce, nontransferable stake: each vertex must lock a deposit before its claims count, and loses part of it if a randomly sampled task exposes fraud. Splitting into many identities does not multiply influence, because each new vertex needs its own deposit and successful history. The vine of trust grows from verified work, not account count; a fake orchard therefore costs the attacker capital, time, and the risk of forfeiture.
